questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which rock edict of Ashoka mentions his personal name 'Devanampiya Piyadasi' for the first time through a separate minor rock edict found at Maski?
questions.explanation: The Minor Rock Edict I found at Maski (Karnataka) is notable because it explicitly mentions the name 'Ashoka' along with the title 'Devanampiya Piyadasi', helping historians conclusively identify Ashoka as the author of the edicts.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Ain-i-Akbari', which provides detailed administrative records of Akbar's reign, was written by which court official?
questions.explanation: Ain-i-Akbari was written by Abul Fazl, one of the Navaratnas of Akbar's court. It forms the third volume of the larger work 'Akbarnama' and covers administration, army, revenues, and social life of the period.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the historic 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution passed on 31 December 1929?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, passed the Purna Swaraj resolution. The tricolour flag was unfurled on the banks of the Ravi river and 26 January was declared as Independence Day.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which Gupta ruler is credited with the title 'Vikramaditya' and is known for defeating the Shakas, as described in the Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II, also known as Vikramaditya, defeated the Western Shakas of Gujarat and Malwa. The Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription (associated with a king named Chandra) is generally attributed to him, and his reign is considered the golden age of the Gupta empire.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Brahmo Samaj', founded in 1828 in Calcutta, aimed at reforming Hinduism by rejecting idol worship and promoting monotheism. Who among the following founded it?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 in Calcutta. He is regarded as the 'Father of Indian Renaissance' and worked against social evils like Sati, while promoting women's rights and rational thinking.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Non-Cooperation Movement formally adopted as a resolution?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was formally adopted at the Nagpur Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920, under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The Dandi March of 1930 was undertaken to protest against which British law or policy?
questions.explanation: Gandhi led the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 to protest the British monopoly on salt production and the Salt Law, which forbade Indians from collecting or selling salt independently.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The slogan 'Do or Die' was given by Mahatma Gandhi in connection with which movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee, launching the Quit India Movement against British rule.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were hanged by the British on which date?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were executed at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931, in connection with the killing of British police officer J.P. Saunders.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Which plan provided the constitutional framework for the partition of British India into India and Pakistan in 1947?
questions.explanation: The Mountbatten Plan of June 1947, also known as the Indian Independence Act 1947, provided the basis for partitioning British India into the two independent dominions of India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to the frequent floods it causes in the state?
questions.explanation: The Kosi river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because it frequently changes its course and causes devastating floods in Bihar every year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The retreating monsoon season in India is associated with which of the following phenomena?
options: Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: During the retreating monsoon (October-November), low-pressure systems form over the Bay of Bengal, leading to tropical cyclones that bring heavy rainfall to the eastern and southern coasts of India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Black soil, which is well known for its ability to retain moisture for long periods, is also called by which name?
questions.explanation: Black soil is also known as Regur soil or cotton soil. It is formed from basaltic lava and is found extensively in the Deccan Plateau. Its high clay content gives it the ability to retain moisture.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is bounded on its west by which mountain range?
questions.explanation: The Deccan Plateau is bounded to the west by the Western Ghats, to the east by the Eastern Ghats, and to the north by the Satpura and Vindhya ranges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following straits connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden?
questions.explanation: The Bab-el-Mandeb strait connects the Red Sea in the north to the Gulf of Aden in the south, and is a crucial waterway between the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea via the Suez Canal.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines 'Gross Domestic Product' (GDP)?
options: Total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents anywhere in the world in a year
Total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's geographic boundary in a given year
Total value of goods and services exported by a country in a year
Net value of all goods and services produced within a country after deducting depreciation
questions.explanation: GDP is defined as the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's geographic boundaries during a specific time period, regardless of the nationality of the producer. Option D describes NDP (Net Domestic Product), not GDP.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The fiscal deficit in the Union Budget of India is expressed as a percentage of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the Union Budget of India. It indicates the total borrowing requirements of the government.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in which year?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, as a private shareholders' bank. It was subsequently nationalised on 1 January 1949, becoming a fully government-owned institution. The year 1969 relates to the nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which type of unemployment is most commonly observed in the agricultural sector of India, where more workers are engaged than actually required?
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment (also called hidden unemployment) occurs when more people are employed on a task than are actually needed, so their marginal productivity is zero or negligible. This is a characteristic feature of the agricultural sector in India.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: If the government's total expenditure exceeds its total receipts excluding borrowings, the difference is called:
questions.explanation: Fiscal Deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts excluding borrowings. It indicates the total amount the government needs to borrow to meet its expenditure. Revenue Deficit pertains only to revenue account, while Primary Deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Constitutional Remedies guaranteed, which Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution grants citizens the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. Ambedkar described it as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because without this remedy, other rights would be meaningless.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51. They are non-justiciable but fundamental to governance. Part IVA deals with Fundamental Duties.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment Act were the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens added to the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976, also known as the 'Mini Constitution', inserted Part IVA (Article 51A) into the Constitution, which lists 10 Fundamental Duties of citizens. The 86th Amendment later added an 11th duty.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Which house of the Indian Parliament is described as a permanent house that cannot be dissolved, and one-third of its members retire every two years?
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution. Its members serve a six-year term, and one-third of them retire every two years, ensuring continuity. The Lok Sabha, in contrast, can be dissolved by the President.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added the Eleventh Schedule to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional recognition to Panchayati Raj institutions by adding Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule (listing 29 subjects) to the Constitution. The 74th Amendment similarly dealt with Urban Local Bodies.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gland in the human body is responsible for regulating the body's metabolic rate by secreting thyroxine hormone?
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland, located in the neck, secretes thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) hormones that directly regulate the body's basal metabolic rate. Deficiency of thyroxine leads to hypothyroidism.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: When a solution of sodium hydroxide reacts with a solution of hydrochloric acid, which products are formed?
questions.explanation: NaOH + HCl ? NaCl + H?O. This is a classic neutralisation reaction between a strong base and a strong acid, producing common salt (sodium chloride) and water.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A person suffering from myopia (short-sightedness) is prescribed spectacles. Which type of lens is used to correct this defect?
questions.explanation: In myopia, the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is used to correct this defect as it diverges the incoming light rays so that they finally focus on the retina.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin leads to the disease called 'Scurvy', characterised by bleeding gums and weakness?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Vitamin C is essential for the synthesis of collagen, and its deficiency leads to bleeding gums, skin hemorrhages, and delayed wound healing.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: According to Newton's third law of motion, when a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun moves backward. This backward movement of the gun is called:
questions.explanation: Newton's third law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. When a bullet is fired forward, the gun experiences an equal and opposite force pushing it backward, known as recoil. This is also consistent with the law of conservation of momentum.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article 25% above its cost price and then gives a discount of 12% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. Marked Price = 125. After 12% discount, SP = 125 ? 0.88 = 110. Profit% = (110 - 100)/100 ? 100 = 10%.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself?
questions.explanation: If principal = P, it doubles in 8 years, so SI = P in 8 years, meaning rate = 100/8 = 12.5% per year. To become 4P, SI needed = 3P. Time = (3P ? 100)/(P ? 12.5) = 24 years.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: The ratio of the ages of Ravi and Suresh is 4 : 5. After 6 years, this ratio will become 6 : 7. What is the present age of Suresh?
questions.explanation: Let present ages be 4x and 5x. After 6 years: (4x+6)/(5x+6) = 6/7. Cross-multiplying: 7(4x+6) = 6(5x+6) => 28x+42 = 30x+36 => 2x = 6 => x = 3. Suresh's age = 5?3 = 15 years.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: Simplify: 840 ? 14 + 3 ? 25 - 120 ? 8
questions.explanation: Following BODMAS: 840 ? 14 = 60; 3 ? 25 = 75; 120 ? 8 = 15. So the expression = 60 + 75 - 15 = 120 - 15... wait: 60 + 75 = 135, then 135 - 15 = 120. Re-check: 60 + 75 - 15 = 120. Correct answer is 120, option A.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive even numbers is 36. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: For 5 consecutive even numbers, the average equals the middle (3rd) number. So the middle number is 36. The 5 numbers are 32, 34, 36, 38, 40. The largest is 40.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct antonym of the word '????'?
questions.explanation: ????' means 'taking/receiving' and its antonym is '??????' meaning 'giving/granting'. The common phrase '????-??????' (give and take / exchange) confirms this.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct meaning of the idiom '????? ??? ????'?
questions.explanation: The idiom '????? ??? ????' means to fall in love or to have eyes meet with affection. It describes the moment two people develop romantic feelings for each other.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: Which Ras (poetic sentiment) is known as the 'King of Ras' (?????) in Hindi poetry?
questions.explanation: Shringar Ras (?????? ??) is called 'Rasraj' (King of Ras) in Hindi poetry. Its Sthayi Bhav (permanent emotion) is 'Rati' (love/attraction).

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the word 'BENEVOLENT'.
questions.explanation: Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly, so 'Charitable' is its closest synonym. 'Malicious' is its antonym, while 'Arrogant' and 'Indifferent' are unrelated.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition: 'She has been working on this project ______ three months.'
questions.explanation: When expressing a duration of time (a span), 'for' is used. 'Since' is used with a specific point in time, not a duration like 'three months'.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the word 'FRUGAL'.
questions.explanation: Frugal' means careful and sparing with money or resources. Its antonym is 'Extravagant', which means spending excessively. 'Thrifty' is actually a synonym of 'Frugal'.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error: 'The committee (A) have reached (B) their decision (C) unanimously. (D) No error'
questions.explanation: Committee' is a collective noun treated as singular in formal/standard grammar, so the correct verb is 'has reached' instead of 'have reached'. This is a common subject-verb agreement error tested in UPSSSC PET.

questions.explanation: Insolvent' precisely means a person who is unable to pay their debts. A 'Miser' is someone who hoards money, a 'Creditor' is one to whom money is owed, and a 'Prodigal' is a person who spends recklessly.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing number in the series: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ?
questions.explanation: The series consists of perfect squares: 2?, 3?, 4?, 5?, 6?, so the next term is 7? = 49.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code language, 'ORANGE' is written as 'TCPUIG'. Following the same rule, how will 'MANGO' be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted +2 positions forward: O?T, R?U, A?C, N?P, G?I, E?G. Similarly for MANGO: M?O, A?C, N?P, G?I, O?Q, giving OCPIQ.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, Suresh says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the person in the photograph related to Suresh?
questions.explanation: Suresh's grandfather's only son is Suresh's father. The daughter of Suresh's father is Suresh's sister.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Ravi starts from point A, walks 8 km towards North, then turns right and walks 6 km, then turns right again and walks 8 km. How far and in which direction is he now from point A?
questions.explanation: Ravi goes North 8 km, then East 6 km, then South 8 km. The northward and southward legs cancel out, leaving him 6 km due East of point A.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are copies. Conclusions: I. Some pens are copies. II. Some copies are books. Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
questions.explanation: Conclusion II directly follows because 'Some books are copies' converts to 'Some copies are books.' Conclusion I does not follow because we cannot link pens directly to copies ? the middle term 'books' is not fully distributed.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Under the PM Vishwakarma scheme, launched by the Government of India, what is the maximum loan amount available in the second tranche to artisans and craftspeople?
questions.explanation: Under PM Vishwakarma, eligible artisans first receive up to Rs. 1 lakh in the first tranche, and up to Rs. 2 lakh in the second tranche, at a concessional interest rate of 5%.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The Padma Vibhushan is the second highest civilian award in India. It is awarded for 'distinguished service of exceptional order.' Which ministry recommends these awards?
questions.explanation: Padma Awards are civilian honours instituted by the Government of India. The Ministry of Home Affairs administers these awards and processes recommendations received from various state governments, central ministries, and individuals.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India became a full member of which grouping in 2023, joining alongside Saudi Arabia, UAE, Ethiopia, Iran, and Argentina (though Argentina later declined)?
questions.explanation: At the BRICS summit in Johannesburg in August 2023, six new countries were invited to join BRICS, including Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iran, Ethiopia, Egypt, and Argentina, with membership effective from January 2024. India is an original BRICS member.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup was hosted by India. Which team won the tournament?
questions.explanation: Australia won the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, defeating India in the final held at Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad on November 19, 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: ISRO's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed on the Moon in August 2023. The lander of this mission was named:
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3's lander was named Vikram, and the rover onboard was named Pragyan. It landed near the lunar south pole on August 23, 2023, making India the first country to achieve a soft landing near the Moon's south pole.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chief Election Commissioner of India in March 2024, following the enactment of the Chief Election Commissioners and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023?
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar was appointed as the Chief Election Commissioner of India in March 2024 under the new appointment process established by the 2023 Act, which replaced the earlier Supreme Court-mandated panel with a committee including the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The new Parliament building of India was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in May 2023. Which historical symbol was installed in the Central Hall of the new Parliament?
questions.explanation: The Sengol, a historical Tamil royal sceptre symbolising the transfer of power, was installed near the Speaker's chair in the new Parliament building during its inauguration on May 28, 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The Uttar Pradesh government launched the 'Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Yojana' primarily to provide free coaching to students preparing for which type of examinations?
options: Competitive exams like IAS, IPS, NDA, CDS
questions.explanation: Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Yojana was launched in Uttar Pradesh on Basant Panchami 2021 to provide free coaching to economically weaker section students for competitive exams such as IAS, IPS, PCS, NDA, CDS, JEE, NEET, and others.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is governed and operated by which organisation?
questions.explanation: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), an umbrella organisation for retail payment systems in India, set up under the guidance of the Reserve Bank of India and the Indian Banks Association.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India officially submitted its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the UNFCCC in 2022, committing to achieve approximately what percentage of cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel based energy resources by 2030?
questions.explanation: India's updated NDC (2022) committed to achieving about 50% of cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel based energy resources by 2030, updating the earlier target of 40% set in the 2015 NDC.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was a policy introduced during the Governor-Generalship of which British official in India?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse was implemented by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. Under this policy, any princely state without a natural male heir would be annexed by the British East India Company.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which river forms the boundary between the states of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh for a significant stretch?
questions.explanation: The Chambal river flows along the border of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh and then forms the boundary between Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh before joining the Yamuna. It is well known for its ravines and forms a natural inter-state boundary.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution can the President of India declare a National Emergency on the ground of armed rebellion?
questions.explanation: Article 352 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to declare a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion. The 44th Constitutional Amendment replaced the earlier term 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan of India adopted the 'Mahalanobis Model' as its economic framework, focusing on heavy industries?
questions.explanation: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956?1961) was based on the Mahalanobis Model, developed by statistician P. C. Mahalanobis. It emphasized rapid industrialization with a focus on heavy and capital goods industries.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which vitamin is produced in the human body when the skin is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Vitamin D, often called the 'sunshine vitamin', is synthesized in the skin when it is exposed to ultraviolet B (UVB) rays from sunlight. It plays a crucial role in calcium absorption and bone health.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which city of Uttar Pradesh is known as the 'City of Nawabs' and is famous for its Chikankari embroidery?
questions.explanation: Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh, is historically known as the 'City of Nawabs' due to its association with the Nawabs of Awadh. It is world-renowned for its Chikankari embroidery, a delicate form of hand embroidery on fabric.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The classical dance form 'Kathak' is primarily associated with which region of India?
questions.explanation: Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance and originates from northern India, primarily from Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow and Varanasi gharanas) and Rajasthan (Jaipur gharana). The word 'Kathak' is derived from 'Katha', meaning story.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Palk Strait' separates India from which neighboring country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait is a narrow body of water that separates the Tamil Nadu coast of southeastern India from the Jaffna Peninsula of northern Sri Lanka. It connects the Bay of Bengal in the north with the Palk Bay in the south.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Dronacharya Award' in India is given to recognize outstanding achievements in which field?
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award, officially known as the Dronacharya Award for Outstanding Coaches in Sports and Games, is a prestigious award given by the Government of India to coaches who have produced medal-winning athletes at prestigious international sports events.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which session of the Indian National Congress first demanded 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) as its goal?
questions.explanation: At the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the resolution for Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) was passed. January 26, 1930 was declared as the first Independence Day, and this date later became India's Republic Day.
